claims.statement: Moria is a reusable Rust voxel-world substrate consumed through public crate interfaces by games and a minimal validation executable; this repository delivers the substrate, not any particular game.

The current product owns deterministic seed-based generation, sparse voxel storage, bounded streaming, mutation, surface extraction, persistence, and read-only diagnostics useful to multiple downstream consumers.

External consumers create and identify a world, request bounded regions, observe readiness, query material truth, submit bounded edits, and persist deltas; the validation executable uses exactly these public interfaces and owns no privileged world path.
Generation is deterministic for the same versioned parameters and seed.

Mutation is admitted through a bounded command API and committed atomically; persistence restores the same authoritative material state; derived meshes and diagnostics never become authoritative world state; streaming bounds resident work with typed observable failures and generation identities.

Headless fixtures cover generation, query, mutation, persistence, and lifecycle behavior; a small visual fixture demonstrates a relocated external consumer through the public API; performance is reported with machine identity without a machine-specific correctness threshold.
Moria does not implement game rules, combat, inventory, AI, narrative systems, characters, animation, authored levels, or production content.

After the reusable substrate ships, a separate Product One repository may place a third-person explorer in a generated region; that later game-facing demo may use skeletal animation and a curated cliff-to-cave traversal, and does not authorize a player controller, character mesh, or animation clips in Moria.

A later Product One consumer vision may include a dense mixed forest among hills, river, and cave content in a separate repository; that forest population workload is future-consumer context and is not authorized in Moria.
Moria is the reusable voxel-world substrate defined by docs/seeds/mixed-project-brief.md; only the current substrate commitments are deliverables in this repository.
docs/seeds/substrate-interface-reference.md supplies supporting technical context without expanding product scope.
The interface reference supports the Moria program brief, describes the reusable surface downstream consumers need, and does not add deliverables.

World identity combines format version, generation parameters, and seed; queries return readiness and bounded authoritative material; mutations are bounded commands with admission failures and commit revisions; streaming exposes lifecycle states; persistence records authoritative deltas rather than derived meshes.
